title: The Broken US Healthcare System is Failing Millions of Americans with Warris Bokhari
summary: Eisman and Warris Bokhari examine denial incentives, insurer ownership of care delivery, Medicare risk coding, Medicaid selection and ACA affordability. The strongest reasoning distinguishes coverage from affordability, identifies float and duration mismatches, and recognizes that a breakup cannot repair underwriting by itself. Several broad conclusions rely on selected cases or mismatched statistics: physician reimbursement becomes a pharmacy comparison, asset depletion becomes bankruptcy, and review expenses become medical spending. Claimable’s success and disruption claims remain founder assertions. No sector stock-return recommendation is inferred.
assessment: Material sector economics and policy mechanisms are retained separately from supporting factual errors. Verified definitions support some reasoning, but neither selected patient harm nor poor stock performance proves a universal deliberate-denial business model. Guest-only allegations are not attributed to Eisman.
speaker_map_notes: Warris Bokhari supplies healthcare cases and policy explanations. Eisman asks clarifying questions and sometimes expressly restates conclusions; only those substantive adoptions are recorded as his claims. Claimable is the guest’s own business and creates a relevant commercial interest.
framework_points: Follow the money across insurance, providers and pharmacies rather than looking only at insurance margins.
Separate patient access, approval, payment and ultimate affordability.
Probe incentives with simplified arithmetic, but avoid letting illustrative margins become measured profits.
Anecdotes motivate hypotheses; population denominators and causal counterfactuals remain essential.
tools_and_charts: Medical loss ratio and administrative expense bridge
transcript_cautions: Published January 12 2026 but ACA-subsidy negotiations and references to this year indicate a likely late-2025 recording; exact recording date is unavailable.
Captions switch to HH:MM:SS after one hour; complete 78-minute transcript was read with corrected timestamp parser.
V28 is discussed as CPT code removal although CMS uses diagnosis/HCC risk mapping.
Caption renders some company names and 85 cents per hundred dollars incorrectly; monetary examples are treated as illustrative.
Founder claims, private patient histories and alleged retaliation lack independently inspected case records.
Opening montage repeats later discussion and is not separately counted.

claims.claim: Roughly 17% of five billion annual healthcare claims are denied, affecting an estimated 70-90 million Americans.
claims.speaker: Warris Bokhari
claims.test: Establish whether the stated national denial extrapolation proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: Marketplace claims data cannot establish all-market claim volume or unique affected people. The conversion from claims to people requires repeat-claim and population information.

evidence.title: Claims denials and appeals in ACA marketplace plans in 2023
evidence.finding: Author analysis of CMS marketplace disclosures, not all commercial insurance. Updated page reports about 20% in-network denials; fewer than 1% appealed and 56% upheld. Initial denials later resubmitted and paid are excluded, but new claims can still secure payment. Claim counts are not unique people.

claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: A one-percent increase in healthcare prices produces roughly two percent more deaths, reflecting addiction and loss of access.
claims.speaker: Warris Bokhari
claims.test: Establish whether the stated healthcare price mortality proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.
claims.reason: The cited research estimates suicide/overdose mortality through labor-market effects, not all deaths or a universal access-to-treatment effect. Approximate magnitude is plausible only within that narrower outcome.

evidence.title: Who pays for rising health care prices? Evidence from hospital mergers
evidence.finding: Instrumental-variable study uses merger-driven price variation. A 1% price rise is associated with 2.7% more suicide and overdose deaths, not all-cause mortality; mechanism includes employer labor costs and job loss. County-level estimates are not a universal clinical elasticity.

evidence.title: Medicare Advantage Medical Loss Ratio
evidence.finding: MA and Part D contract-level MLR must be at least 85%; violations can require remittances to CMS, enrollment restrictions and termination. MLR is a regulatory patient-care measure, not simply GAAP gross or net profit; it is not a universal 15% net-margin cap.

claims.reason: Loss follows only if other net expenses exceed the remaining premium margin. A 91% care ratio with 5% administration and no other items yields 4% underwriting profit. Ninety percent is not a universal threshold.

evidence.title: Emergency room rights under EMTALA
evidence.finding: Covered emergency departments must screen and stabilize qualifying emergencies regardless of ability to pay. This is an access duty, not insurance coverage or a general prohibition on subsequent bills.

evidence.title: Death or Debt? National estimates of financial toxicity
evidence.publisher: Gilligan et al., American Journal of Medicine
evidence.finding: Indexed author abstract reports 42.4% complete asset depletion at two years in Health and Retirement Study participants, mean age 68.6, using 1998-2014 data. This is not 50% of all cancer patients filing bankruptcy. Full article access returned 403; abstract findings only.

evidence.title: Cancer diagnosis and bankruptcy registry study
evidence.finding: Linked Washington cancer registry and court filings: 2.2% of 197840 patients filed over observation; 0.52% within one year, about 1.7% within five. Regional historical cohort cannot determine current national incidence, but formal bankruptcy is distinct from asset depletion.
